title: Thermal rollout notes and pin strategy (scratch)
content:
Context / purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for the upcoming model flip (v2025.11 -> v2025.12). Trying a "thermal" ramp approach: small, rapid heating pulses with cooldown checkpoints rather than a single continuous % ramp.
- Goal: get to 20% stable within 6 hours, then evaluate quality regressions + cost. If stable, open to 50% by EOD; otherwise hold and iterate.

High-level constraints / non-negotiables:
- SLO: P95 < 350ms for hosted customers on m-latency tier. If P95 spikes > 25% over baseline for two consecutive 5m windows, pause ramp and backoff to last stable version.
- Cost cap for experiment: +15% token cost relative to baseline (rolling 4h). If exceeded, throttle via batching/quantization route.
- Data sensitivity: no unredacted customer PII to be used in evals; QA dataset in GH private must be used.

Thermal ramp plan (working):
1) Preflight (T-minus 90m):
   - Smoke deploy v2025.12 to staging dedicated pool; run end-to-end test harness (long prompt leakage, KV cache reuse, streaming). Ticket JIRA-3142.
   - Run quick eval suite (50 prompts) — acceptance criteria: exact-match rate >= baseline - 0.5% (for key intents).
   - Notify #releases and #oncall at +60m and +15m.

2) Pulse 0 (initial heating) — 1% traffic, 10 minutes:
   - Purpose: verify routing and decluster hooks, ensure logs/trace paths intact.
   - Check: trace ids present, sampling 1:10 for full logs.
   - Abort if any 5xx or elevated error ratio > 0.5% in 10m window.

3) Pulse 1 — 3% traffic, 20 minutes (after 10m cooldown):
   - Run signal checks at 5m and 20m marks:
     * Latency P50/P95/P99 compared to baseline (alert if P95 > baseline*1.25)
     * Model quality quick-check: prompt subset run and compare BLEU/intent-match
     * Error rate, streaming disconnects, token truncation events.
   - If any signal fails -> backoff to 1% or rollback.

4) Pulse 2 — 8% traffic, 30 minutes (after cooldown):
   - Increase sampling of full logs to 1:5.
   - Run parallel A/B user-flow synthetic tests (login -> chat -> save). Verify downstream metrics (DB write latency, webhook success).

5) Thermal hold — 1h observation at 8%:
   - This is a deliberate longer cooldown to catch slow-failure modes (memory leaks, KV cache saturation).
   - If steady, proceed to 20% ramp.

6) Ramp to 20% (stepped: 12% -> 16% -> 20% in 15min increments)
   - At each step run full metric checklist. If anything marginal, stop and escalate to oncall.

7) Post-rollout acceptance window (4h):
   - Run full regression eval suite (1k prompts) on production traffic sample (anonymized).
   - Run "quality regression delta" dashboard; threshold: no more than 1% regression on intent-pass and no critical hallucination pattern increase (manual triage for unusual tokens).

Pin & fallback logic (notes to self):
- Pinging approach: for customers who requested stable model pinning we must honor tenant-level pins. Use route-filters to maintain tenant pins when flipping default.
- Implementation: add model alias "stable-2025-11" -> points to v2025.11. Default alias flips to v2025.12 for global traffic. Tenants with pinned alias remain unaffected.
- Quick rollback command (CLI):
    redwood route set-default --alias stable-2025-11 --force --reason "thermal rollback - <short reason>"
- Quick pin command to rescue a tenant mid-ramp:
    redwood tenant pin --tenant-id <id> --alias stable-2025-11

Safety thresholds (machine readable rules):
- LatencyAbort: P95 > baseline*1.25 for two consecutive 5m windows.
- ErrorAbort: error_rate > 0.5% in 10m window.
- CostAbort: 4h rolling cost delta > 15% above baseline.
- QualityAbort: intent-fail delta > 1.0% on regression suite of 1k samples.
- OperationalAbort: streaming disconnects > 0.8% or DB write failures > 0.2%.

Emergency flow (fast path):
- Oncall receives Slack ping via #releases (urgent) and page if P95 or error triggers.
- If emergency: flip default alias to stable-2025-11, notify engineering, open incident ticket, start live debug (logs/heapdump).
- If partial degradation (single region): shift traffic away from region, place a region-level fallback to cheaper/older variant.

Telemetry + dashboards to watch (quick checklist):
- model.latency.{p50,p95,p99} (per-route, per-region)
- model.errors.total + model.errors.5xx
- cost.per-token.rolling_1h
- quality.intent_pass.delta (A/B eval)
- stream.disconnects.count
- kvcache.hit_ratio (watch for sudden drop -> cache thrashing)
- infra.gpu_mem_utilization (OOM risk)

Open questions / what to validate in next dry-run:
- How does batching change under higher sequence length workloads? Does thermal pulsing create queuing artifacts?
- Do SDKs gracefully surface alias flips to long-lived SDK sessions? Need to test client pinned sessions.
- Verify tenant pinning respects sub-route overrides (support-team asked about edge cases).

Local quick tests (commands):
- smoke generate: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"alias:v2025.12","prompt":"QA smoke"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- flip default alias: redwood route set-default --alias alias:v2025.12 --dry-run
- simulate heat: run loadtest/local_heat.py --qps 50 --seq-len 1024 --duration 15m

Notes to self / reminders:
- Push the lightweight canary logs gating rule into the console so product can watch live during warmup.
- Ask SRE for a transient increase in log retention for the 8% -> 20% window (need 72h for triage).
- Coordinate with CS for high-value tenants who want early opt-in; prepare a short FAQ and toggle instructions.

Rough timeline (today):
- T-90m: staging smoke + notify
- T-60m: run QA suite, oncall aware
- T-0: Pulse 0 -> follow thermal plan above -> aim 20% by +6h

If anything feels off mid-run: stop. Cool down 30-60m. Talk to Leah (telemetry) and Priya (CS) before continuing.

End of scratch. This is messy by design. Will copy relevant parts to the release checklist doc and to the release runbook once validated.
